plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: Arching, jointed green stems drip with satiny, asymmetrical blossoms in shades of pink, magenta and white. Each bloom hangs like a little lantern from the tips of the branches. It gives a burst of tropical colour just as winter sets in.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter, beginning around Thanksgiving in North America (late November) and continuing into the new year
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil, and widely grown as a houseplant in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Christmas cacti are not desert plants. In the wild they grow as epiphytes, perching on tree branches in misty Brazilian forests. Shortening autumn days trigger their buds.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub flowers when most gardens are fading. Its delicately scented blooms, with 6–8 petals and a boss of golden stamens, open in white, pale pink or rich rose and scatter petals like confetti beneath the branches. Bees and other pollinators visit on mild winter days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (roughly October through December or later, depending on climate)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan and the Ryukyu Islands, and grown in mild-winter gardens across Asia, Europe, Australia and the southern United States
plants.funFact: The leaves of its close relative, Camellia sinensis, are used to make tea. Sasanqua seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: The brilliant red 'petals' are actually colourful leaves, called bracts, that surround clusters of tiny golden-yellow flowers. In warm climates it grows into a rangy shrub several metres tall, lighting up winter landscapes. Cultivated varieties also come in pink, cream, orange and speckled forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, with the main show in November and December
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America, now grown in frost-free gardens and as a potted holiday plant worldwide
plants.funFact: What looks like a single flower is really a cluster of tiny cup-shaped structures called cyathia. The showy colour comes from the bracts around them. The plant is named for Joel Roberts Poinsett, the first U.S. ambassador to Mexico, who introduced it to the United States in the 1820s.
